inputs.source: On-call engineer's chat request, authenticated via company SSO

instructions.note: The agent deploys or migrates whatever service or migration is named, with no stated validation of scope or appropriateness.
Explicit instruction to skip confirmation before irreversible production actions grants the agent unilateral authority under the engineer's identity.

controls.name: Cloud provider audit logging of production actions
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the cloud platform outside the model; does not weaken as the model gets more capable, but it only records after the fact and attributes every action to the engineer's identity, so it cannot by itself show whether the agent or the human acted.

controls.name: Human approval gate before irreversible or production-impacting actions
controls.decay_rationale: Recommended as a raw-action review gate enforced in the orchestration layer, not the model; would not decay with model capability if the approver reviews the actual migration script and deploy target rather than a model summary.

controls.name: Agent-specific service identity distinct from the engineer's personal credential
controls.decay_rationale: A separately issued, scoped service identity for the agent would be enforced at the identity provider, not the model, and would let the audit log distinguish agent-initiated calls from the engineer's own direct actions.

controls.name: Tamper-evident record of the request and rationale, independent of the user-deletable chat transcript
controls.decay_rationale: Would be written to a store the requesting engineer cannot delete, closing the gap where the only record of why an action was requested can be erased by the same person who requested it.

controls.name: Pre-migration backup and rollback capability
controls.decay_rationale: A backup taken before migration is enforced by infrastructure, not the model, and would bound the consequence of a mistaken or hijacked migration.

findings.title: Shared engineer credential and deletable intent record defeat accountability for agent-executed production actions (ASI09, STRIDE repudiation)

attack_path.note: Engineer asks the agent to deploy or migrate; this request exists only in the chat transcript.
The chat transcript is the only record of what was asked and why. The engineer who asked can delete it.
The agent performs the irreversible migration using the engineer's own personal access token.
The cloud log records the action under the engineer's identity only; it does not show that an agent, rather than the engineer directly, took the action, or why.

forecast.watch_signal: Autonomy is raised (for example, migrations run on a schedule or without a per-request engineer trigger) without adding a distinct agent identity, or cloud audit logging is disabled or narrowed.

evidence.observation: The agent uses the on call engineer's personal access token, passed in at session start, for every production action.
Every production action is recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name, with no indication the log distinguishes agent-executed actions from the engineer's own.
The chat transcript is the only record of what the agent was asked and why, and engineers can delete their own chat history.

recommendations.action: Issue the agent its own scoped service identity for production actions, separate from any engineer's personal token, so the audit log can distinguish agent-executed actions from the engineer acting directly.
Write an append-only, engineer-undeletable record of each request (who, what, when, why) alongside the resulting action, so intent cannot be erased by the requester after the fact.

findings.title: Irreversible production database migration executes with no human approval gate (ASI02)

attack_path.note: Engineer names a migration to run in production.
The agent runs it immediately; the prompt explicitly forbids asking for confirmation, and the migration cannot be rolled back automatically.

threat_refs.name: Data Destruction via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: Migration scope expands to additional production databases, or the agent is allowed to run migrations without any per-request engineer trigger.

evidence.observation: "deploy the named service or run the named migration in production using the engineer's credentials" gives the agent an unconditional path to run migrations.
"Do not ask for confirmation; the engineer is busy" removes any human checkpoint before the action runs.
"Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically," confirming the action is irreversible.

recommendations.action: Require a human approval step before running a production database migration, with the approver shown the actual migration script and target, not a model-generated summary.
Take an automatic backup or snapshot immediately before each migration so a bad migration can be reversed.

findings.title: Production deployment executes with no human approval gate (ASI02)

attack_path.note: Engineer names a service to deploy.
The agent deploys immediately using the engineer's credentials, with no confirmation step.

forecast.watch_signal: The deploy credential scope widens from the engineer's own delegated token to a shared or broad service credential, or deploy targets expand to systems holding restricted data.

evidence.observation: The agent deploys the named service using the engineer's credentials and is instructed not to ask for confirmation.
The deploy action runs with the on call engineer's personal access token rather than a scoped service credential.

recommendations.action: Require approval before deploying to production targets classified as high impact, or add automatic rollback on failed health checks.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is high: the agent runs an irreversible production database migration (and a partially reversible deployment) on a trusted, SSO-authenticated request, with no step or runtime limits declared, which triggers the autonomy modifier. Residual risk stays high because the only active control is a detective cloud audit log; the design credits no preventive control, since the system prompt explicitly forbids confirmation and audit entries are not separated from the engineer's own actions, which defeats accountability (ASI09) on top of the unreviewed irreversible migration (ASI02). Forecast risk reaches critical if autonomy increases or audit logging is removed, because the identity and accountability gap would then compound with no detective backstop left at all. The single control whose decay matters most is the cloud audit log (ctl.cloud_audit_log): it is independent of the model, but it already attributes every action to the engineer alone, so losing it removes the last signal that anything happened.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in the provided system prompt and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.

No tool manifest, MCP configuration, or IaC was provided; capability properties (action, reversibility, credential scope) are inferred from prose rather than verified, so confidence on exact sink classification is medium to high rather than verified.

The exact breadth of the engineer's personal access token is not documented; it is recorded as credential_scope 'user_delegated' per the schema vocabulary, with its effective severity treated as a judgment call noted in finding evidence rather than a confirmed fact.
